Title: Arbitrary Command Execution / Code Injection in Generated PowerShell Autocomplete Script via Invoke-Expression
Analysis:
In spf13/cobra, the generated powershell completion script uses `Invoke-Expression` to execute a command that obtains the completion results from the target Go binary. Specifically, it builds the `$RequestComp` variable by concatenating the raw command-line arguments typed by the user (stored in the `$Arguments` string) without any sanitization or escaping of PowerShell metacharacters:

`$RequestComp="$Program %[3]s $Arguments"`

This command is then executed via `Invoke-Expression`:

`Invoke-Expression -OutVariable out "$RequestComp" 2>&1 | Out-Null`

If a user pastes a command line containing PowerShell metacharacters (such as `;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks, or other PowerShell code blocks) and triggers completion, the shell will evaluate and execute that code during the `Invoke-Expression` call.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
Pasting or typing the following command line in a PowerShell session with cobra completion active:
`mycobraapp subcmd "foo; id; "`
And then pressing `<TAB>` to trigger completion will cause PowerShell to execute the `id` command (or any arbitrary command specified).
The `$RequestComp` variable evaluated by PowerShell will be:
`mycobraapp __complete subcmd "foo; id; "`
Which parses as two separate commands split by the semicolon `;`:
1. `mycobraapp __complete subcmd "foo`
2. `id`
3. `"`
Thus, the `id` command executes in the context of the user's PowerShell shell.
Snippet:
#call the command store the output in $out and redirect stderr and stdout to null
    # $Out is an array contains each line per element
    Invoke-Expression -OutVariable out "$RequestComp" 2>&1 | Out-Null

Title: Arbitrary Command Execution / Code Injection in Generated Fish Autocomplete Script via eval
Analysis:
In spf13/cobra, the generated fish shell completion script uses `eval` to execute a command that obtains the completion results from the target Go binary. Specifically, it builds the `requestComp` variable by concatenating the raw command-line arguments typed by the user (stored in the shell's `args` list) without any sanitization or escaping of shell metacharacters:

`set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $args[2..-1] $lastArg"`

This command is then executed via `eval`:

`set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)`

If a user pastes a command line containing shell metacharacters (such as `;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, or backticks) and triggers completion (manually via TAB or automatically), the shell will execute those metacharacters during the `eval` call. Additionally, if the user triggers autocomplete in a directory containing files named with metacharacters (e.g., `$(touch pwned)`), these can also be executed when the completed word is parsed.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
Pasting or typing the following command line in fish:
`mycobraapp subcmd "foo; id; "`
And then pressing `<TAB>` to trigger completion will cause the shell to execute the `id` command.
The `requestComp` variable evaluated by fish will be:
`COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP=0 mycobraapp __complete subcmd "foo; id; "`
Which parses as two separate commands split by the semicolon `;`:
1. `COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP=0 mycobraapp __complete subcmd "foo`
2. `id`
3. `"`
Thus, the `id` command executes in the context of the user's shell.
Snippet:
# Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $args[2..-1] $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)
